learner_notice: Commit one response before feedback appears. Entry checks are low stakes; an unresolved fresh re-entry returns control without exit credit.

items.title: Starting check: norm versus sanction
items.prompt: A club expects members to silence phones during meetings. A member who complies receives public praise. What is the praise?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Guided practice: routine convention
items.prompt: Guests are expected to stand in an orderly queue. A person who cuts receives annoyed looks but no formal penalty. Which norm category is the closest fit?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Less help: moral importance
items.prompt: A community treats care for dependent family members as a strong moral obligation and responds to abandonment with severe condemnation. Which category fits best?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: On your own: intense prohibition
items.prompt: A behavior is treated as profoundly prohibited and evokes near-universal, intense condemnation in the described group. Which norm type is closest?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Near exit: classify the response
items.prompt: A licensing board suspends a member for violating a written professional rule. How should the suspension be classified?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Changed exit: identify system-level anomie
items.prompt: After rapid institutional change, residents report that old expectations no longer apply, new expectations conflict, and enforcement is unpredictable. Which concept best fits?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: expectation before response
items.prompt: Which sequence correctly analyzes a norm-and-sanction vignette?
options: Name punishment → assume taboo → ignore rule
Identify one violator → conclude anomie → stop
Classify reward as norm → omit expectation
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: positive formal response
items.prompt: A university awards an official certificate for compliance with a service expectation. What is the certificate?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: anomie evidence
items.prompt: Which observation most directly supports anomie?
options: One member receives a mild reminder about etiquette.
A board applies a written penalty consistently.
A group strongly condemns a prohibited behavior.
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: conflicting expectations
items.prompt: Two institutions governing the same role issue incompatible expectations, and neither can reliably enforce its rules. Which concept applies?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Starting check: learned definitions
items.prompt: A newcomer learns a prohibited technique and justifications for using it through repeated interaction with close peers. Which theory best fits?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Guided practice: reaction to a label
items.prompt: After a minor violation, a person is publicly labeled dangerous, excluded from conventional roles, and later joins similarly excluded peers. Which theory centers this pathway?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Less help: goals and means
items.prompt: A culture strongly promotes financial success, but a group has sharply restricted access to approved routes for achieving it. Which theory emphasizes the resulting pressure?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: On your own: theory-specific prediction
items.prompt: Which result most directly supports differential association?
options: Behavior changes only after an official label is applied.
Behavior rises where approved means are blocked despite shared goals.
Behavior is identical regardless of peer contact.
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Near exit: locate the mechanism
items.prompt: A student’s conduct changes after teachers repeatedly apply a deviant label and remove access to ordinary school roles. Which explanation is most direct?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Changed exit: choose discriminating evidence
items.prompt: Which observation best separates differential association from labeling theory?
options: A norm exists and some people violate it.
A violation receives a negative sanction.
The behavior occurs in a large city.
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: three causal cues
items.prompt: Which cue belongs to strain theory?
options: Opportunities changed after a public label
Mild disapproval of a routine convention
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: blocked route
items.prompt: A group endorses the same educational goal as others but faces systematic barriers to approved paths for reaching it. Which theory predicts pressure for alternative adaptation?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: make predictions diverge
items.prompt: Which finding most directly favors labeling over strain theory?
options: Behavior varies with access to approved means before any label.
Peers teach techniques before institutions react.
A strong norm receives a strong sanction.
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: compare two pathways
items.prompt: Group A changes behavior after peer instruction; Group B changes only after public classification closes conventional roles. Which pairing fits?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Starting check: rapid short-lived spread
items.prompt: A style spreads quickly through imitation, peaks, and largely disappears within weeks. No norm violation is stated. Which concept fits best?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Guided practice: norm-relative behavior
items.prompt: A person deliberately violates a clearly stated group norm while acting alone, and no broader group process follows. Which construct is directly established?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Less help: socially spreading fear
items.prompt: An unverified odor report moves through a crowd; fear and similar symptoms escalate through observation and rumor despite no detected hazard. Which example is closest?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: On your own: volatile crowd action
items.prompt: A gathering rapidly shifts into convergent crowd action, property damage, and conflict with authorities. Which collective example is closest?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Near exit: use both axes
items.prompt: A coordinated protest follows established rules and spreads through peer networks. Which interpretation is best supported?
options: Deviance only because the event is collective
Riot because all protests are riots
Anomie because people act in a group
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Changed exit: classify a two-case matrix
items.prompt: Case A is a solitary norm violation. Case B is a rapidly spreading group practice with no stated violation. Which pairing is correct?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: two-axis question
items.prompt: Which question identifies deviance rather than collective behavior?
options: How did behavior spread through the group?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: solitary violation
items.prompt: One employee knowingly violates a clear workplace norm in private. No imitation or crowd process occurs. Which classification is supported?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: identify the collective process
items.prompt: Which feature most specifically supports a fad?
options: One person violates a strong norm.
A formal board imposes a penalty.
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: distinguish group processes
items.prompt: A rumor about contamination spreads through a school, and fear-related complaints cluster despite negative environmental tests. Which collective example fits?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Starting check: workplace socialization
items.prompt: A new employee learns an organization’s reporting role through onboarding, shadowing, and supervisor feedback. Which agent is most immediate?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Guided practice: family transmission
items.prompt: Caregivers repeatedly model a greeting routine, prompt children to practice it, and praise its use. Which process is shown?
options: Workplace socialization of an occupational role
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Less help: media scripts
items.prompt: Repeated programs portray one occupation using the same role script, and viewers report learning what that occupation is expected to do. Which agent is central?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: On your own: peer feedback
items.prompt: A student adopts a group-specific speaking style after repeated interaction, imitation, and feedback from friends. Which agent is most direct?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Near exit: identify all three parts
items.prompt: A supervisor demonstrates a safety script, a trainee rehearses it, and correct use becomes part of the trainee’s role identity. Which mapping is correct?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Changed exit: compare conflicting agents
items.prompt: Family messages favor one career role, while peer feedback and media examples favor another. What is the best socialization interpretation?
options: The conflict proves anomie in the whole society.
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: agent–mechanism–outcome
items.prompt: Which mapping is complete?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: media outcome
items.prompt: An online series repeatedly models a new interaction script, and viewers begin using parts of it in conversation. Which mapping fits?
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: identify direct and reinforcing agents
items.prompt: A child first learns a routine from caregivers and later receives matching peer approval. Which statement is most precise?
options: Peers introduced the norm before any family contact.
Media is the only agent because approval is public.
The routine is inherited rather than socialized.
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: workplace and peers
items.prompt: Formal onboarding teaches a communication rule, while coworkers’ daily feedback shapes how it is enacted. Which interpretation fits?
options: Mass media alone determines the role.
Family alone transmits the job rule.
No socialization occurs because two agents are involved.
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.
